title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Evaluating Responses - Minor Informalities
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A vendor submits their physical bid on time and meets all material requirements, but provides three copies of the bid instead of the four requested in the instructions. How should the procurement officer handle this?
options: Waive the issue as a minor informality or irregularity, as it does not affect price, quantity, or quality
Reject the bid as entirely non-responsive
Penalize the vendor's final evaluation score by 5 points
Cancel the solicitation and re-bid to ensure fairness
questions.explain: A minor informality is an error or omission that does not prejudice other bidders or materially affect the price, quality, quantity, or delivery of the goods/services. It can and should be waived by the agency.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A vendor forgets to sign and return the acknowledgment form for Addendum #3. Addendum #3 only contained a correction to a misspelled word in the background section of the IFB. What is the standard action?
options: Reject the bid as strictly non-responsive
Waive the failure to acknowledge the addendum as a minor informality since it had no impact on price, quantity, quality, or delivery
Delay the award for 30 days to allow them to sign it
Deduct the cost of the addendum from their bid
questions.explain: While failing to acknowledge material addenda causes a bid to be non-responsive, an addendum that is purely administrative or informational (like fixing a typo) can be waived as a minor informality.
